title: A move to the OS trash must never be able to become a permanent delete
rule: When code sends a user file to the OS trash, make every path where the OS would delete for good fail before anything happens, and report it as 'no trash' with the file left in place. On Windows, do not rely on a fixed-drive check or on FOF_WANTNUKEWARNING (a prompt the user can answer Yes to): use IFileOperation with FOFX_RECYCLEONDELETE and a progress sink whose PreDeleteItem returns E_ABORT unless TSF_DELETE_RECYCLE_IF_POSSIBLE is set. Keep the decision in a pure function (drive type, sink flags) and unit-test that only the recycle case passes.
rationale: E8.3 (#88): the Recycle Bin move used SHFileOperationW with FOF_WANTNUKEWARNING; on a fixed drive whose bin was off or too small, Windows asked 'permanently delete?', Yes destroyed the file, and the app then reported it as 'could not be moved' with no undo. The drive guard had no test.
